findings.evidence: ModuleDecomposition.lean:54-59 cites only the roadmap. The house convention in the same directory is roadmap + textbook: PathAlgebra.lean:89-90, Radical.lean:91-92, SemisimpleQuotient.lean:72-73, Representation/Comparison.lean:80-81, Representation/Indecomposable.lean:73-74, Kronecker/PathAlgebra.lean:33-35 all cite Assem--Simson--Skowroński Ch. II/III; the roadmap README's References section (lines 479+) lists ASS, Etingof et al., Schiffler, Derksen--Weyman for exactly this layer.
findings.fix: Add the textbook citation to the References section, e.g. "See Assem--Simson--Skowroński, *Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras I*, Ch. III (the equivalence rep_k(Q) ≃ mod kQ)", or Schiffler, *Quiver Representations*, Ch. 5 — both are already in the roadmap's own References list.
findings.issue: The file formalizes the standard equivalence between representations of Q and left kQ-modules in the module ↦ representation direction (its own docstring: "This is the direction 'module ↦ representation' of the equivalence between representations of `Q` and left `kQ`-modules"), including the textbook construction — vertex components eᵥM, paths acting by left multiplication, orientation convention. The References section cites only the roadmap README, naming no source for the theorem itself.

findings.evidence: Module.lean:57-63 References contains only the roadmap link; the Mathlib credit at lines 25-29 covers the ambient API (`CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents`, `DirectSum.completeOrthogonalIdempotents_idempotent`, both confirmed at Mathlib/RingTheory/Idempotents.lean and Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Idempotents.lean:43) but not the statement being formalized.
findings.fix: Name the classical source in one line, e.g. T. Y. Lam, *A First Course in Noncommutative Rings*, §21 (Peirce decomposition), or Assem--Simson--Skowroński I, Ch. I.4, alongside the existing roadmap pointer.
findings.issue: Same omission in the general file: M = ⨁ᵢ eᵢM for a complete orthogonal family of idempotents is the classical Peirce decomposition of a module, and the References section names only the roadmap and the Mathlib declarations consumed.

summary: Mathlib dependencies and the roadmap target are credited and nothing is vendored, but the textbook source of the mathematics is unnamed in both new files: the module-to-representation half of rep_k(Q) ≃ mod kQ is a named theorem the file follows step for step, and every sibling file in TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/ citing this material names Assem--Simson--Skowroński.
